summary: Under Presidential Decree 189/23, the SME eVisa FAQ says nationals of the countries it lists — among them the United Kingdom, the United States, China and Japan — are exempt from tourist visa requirements for stays of up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per year, and that Mozambique, Namibia, São Tomé and Príncipe, South Africa and Zambia are also exempt for short stays under bilateral agreements. For a visa, the FAQ says the visa can only be granted after a visit to the consulate, including an interview and biometric data collection. WHO lists proof of yellow fever vaccination as required for all travellers aged 9 months or over.

tips.text: The SME eVisa FAQ says that, under Presidential Decree 189/23, nationals of the countries it lists are exempt from tourist visa requirements for stays of up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per year.

WHO lists Angola as requiring proof of yellow fever vaccination from all travellers aged 9 months or over, and the SME eVisa FAQ's tourism-visa requirements ask for a valid international vaccination certificate.

The UK Foreign Office says you can take out up to 50,000 kwanzas in cash in addition to foreign currency; the Government of Canada says kwanzas cannot be taken out of the country, and that involvement in black-market currency conversion could lead to arrest.
Canada's travel advice says many doctors and medical staff, including in Luanda, do not speak English or French; they speak Portuguese.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Angola?
faq.answer: Under Presidential Decree 189/23, the SME eVisa FAQ says nationals of the countries it lists — among them the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, China and Japan — are exempt from tourist visa requirements for stays of up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per year, and that Mozambique, Namibia, São Tomé and Príncipe, South Africa and Zambia are also exempt for short stays under bilateral agreements. The SME calls its eVisa site its official portal for tourism and business visas; the FAQ says the online service only collects the application, and that the visa can only be granted after a visit to the consulate, including an interview and biometric data collection.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Angola visa-free?
faq.answer: The SME eVisa FAQ says nationals of the countries on its exemption list may stay up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per year, and that a tourist visa allows a stay of up to 30 days and can be extended once for an equal period.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Angola?
faq.answer: Yes — WHO lists Angola as requiring proof of yellow fever vaccination from all travellers aged 9 months or over.

faq.question: How does the Angola eVisa work?
faq.answer: The SME eVisa FAQ says the online service only collects your application and delivers it to the SME, and that the visa can only be granted after a visit to the consulate, including an interview, biometric data collection and visa fee payment. Its tourism-visa requirements give the visa fee as 36,600.00 KZ paid in cash at the border. The portal's home page says applications are processed in 72 hours and that, if approved, the entry visa is sent by email and must be presented on arrival in Angola.

faq.question: What documents do I need at the Angolan border?
faq.answer: The SME eVisa FAQ's form instructions ask for a passport valid for a minimum of one year with at least 4 empty pages; the UK Foreign Office says your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive in Angola and have at least 2 blank pages; and WHO lists proof of yellow fever vaccination as required for all travellers aged 9 months or over. The SME portal lists a round-trip flight booking, an accommodation booking in Angola and proof of financial means to support the stay among the documents to prepare for a visa application.

levies.name: Special Contribution for Tourism (Contribuição Especial para o Turismo)
levies.exemptions: Domestic tourists and all international tourists under 12 years of age.
levies.text: International tourists (non-resident foreigners) staying in tourist establishments or local accommodation pay 5% of the nightly rate for each night, up to 7 nights. The establishment collects it when the bill is settled, at check-in or check-out. Domestic tourists and international tourists under 12 are exempt. The decree enters into force 90 days after publication.
